headline: TOCVAN DRILLS 81m AT 0.48 G/T AU AT EL MEZQUITE — 47.7m OF 0.80 G/T CONFIRMS GRAN PILAR DISCOVERY IN SONORA
snippet: Tocvan Ventures Corp. (CSE:TOC) reported September 16 that hole JES-26-172 at the El Mezquite trend of the Gran Pilar Gold-Silver Project in Sonora, Mexico returned 81.1 metres grading 0.48 g/t gold from 13.5 metres depth, including 47.7 metres of 0.80 g/t gold and a high-grade core of 2.75 metres at 8.44 g/t gold and 54.0 g/t silver — confirming near-surface mineralisation on the trend and building on discovery hole JES-26-155 (215 metres of 0.6 g/t Au from 36.6m), with step-out JES-26-169 extending known mineralisation approximately 100 metres further north toward a growing corridor management is tracking for an initial resource estimate.

headline: CONTANGO CONFIRMS TORBRIT-NORTH STAR SILVER LINK — 506 G/T AGEQ OVER 13.9m UNIFIES TWO B.C. GOLDEN TRIANGLE DEPOSITS INTO ONE SYSTEM
snippet: Contango Silver & Gold Inc. (NYSE American:CTGO) announced September 15 that systematic step-out drilling between the Torbrit and North Star silver deposits at Kitsault Valley in British Columbia's Golden Triangle has defined a clear structural connection between the two deposits — with initial assays including 506 g/t silver equivalent over 13.90 metres at Torbrit and 807 g/t AgEq over 4.96 metres at North Star — proving they form a single, interconnected silver system, a development CEO Rick Van Nieuwenhuyse says 'opens the door to a unified mine plan and substantially larger resource footprint' within the 50,000-metre 2026 drill program.

headline: SAUDI ARABIA ANNOUNCES 110MT URANIUM ORE BODY IN MADINAH — KINGDOM SIGNALS ENTRY INTO NUCLEAR FUEL SUPPLY CHAIN
snippet: Saudi Arabia announced September 14 the discovery of approximately 110 million tonnes of uranium-concentrated ore in the Madinah region, according to the government's geological survey — a disclosure that coincides with Riyadh's accelerating nuclear energy program and ongoing talks with Western governments for enrichment technology agreements. Analysts will be watching whether the deposit's grade and recovery economics support a long-term domestic fuel processing program, and what the find signals about Saudi Arabia's ambitions within the broader global uranium supply chain.

headline: STORM EXPLORATION FIRES FIRST HOLES AT GOLD STANDARD — 1,500m VMS PROGRAM TARGETS FORGOTTEN INCO CONDUCTOR IN ONTARIO
snippet: Storm Exploration Inc. (TSXV:STRM) announced September 16 the start of its first diamond drill program at the Gold Standard Project 60 kilometres north of Fort Frances, Ontario — targeting an extensive Volcanogenic Massive Sulphide conductor originally identified by Inco and now re-evaluated through modern airborne VTEM and ground VLF geophysics. The up to 1,500-metre, 10-hole program will test the north-south arm of the conductor over a 2-kilometre strike length to confirm VMS-type mineralisation, with drilling scheduled to complete by September 27 before the traditional First Nations moose hunt.

headline: LAHONTAN DRILLS 16.5m AT 2.72 G/T AU IN HISTORIC HEAP LEACH PAD — SANTA FE NEVADA REPROCESSING ECONOMICS TAKE SHAPE
snippet: Lahontan Gold Corp. (TSXV:LG) reported September 15 results from Sonic core drilling at Santa Fe Mine's Heap Leach Pad Two in Nevada, with the best hole returning 16.5 metres grading 2.72 g/t gold and 2.8 g/t silver — approximately 8.5 times the estimated residual grade — while ten completed holes averaged 0.50 g/t gold versus an estimated 0.29 g/t residual; cyanide gold analyses running at 40% of fire assay values suggest the material may respond to conventional cyanide reprocessing, pointing toward a potentially low-capex recovery pathway across all four historic heap leach pads where 86 additional Sonic holes have now been completed.

headline: COPPER POSTS FIRST WEEKLY LOSS SINCE JUNE AS WHITE HOUSE SHELVES TARIFF PLAN — FREEPORT, SOUTHERN COPPER, TECK EACH DROP 7%
snippet: Copper settled at US$14,233 a tonne on September 12, ending its first losing week since June after Reuters reported that Washington had shelved plans to impose tariffs on imported refined copper, citing concerns about manufacturing cost impacts ahead of the midterm elections; the metal had briefly touched a record US$14,875 before the news hit. Freeport-McMoRan fell 6.6%, Southern Copper dropped 7.2%, and Teck Resources declined 6.8% on the session — though structural tightness from Grasberg running at 65% capacity and Escondida grade declining toward 0.70% means the tariff uncertainty is dictating near-term price swings more than the underlying supply-demand math.

headline: URANIUM MINERS 15-20 YEARS BEHIND DEMAND CURVE — STRUCTURAL DEFICIT WIDENS TOWARD 18% SUPPLY SHORTFALL BY 2027
snippet: Mining.com's September 16 chart analysis examines the widening gap between uranium mine development timelines and accelerating reactor build programs, finding that global exploration and development spending — up 46% to US$1.78 billion in 2023-2024 — cannot meaningfully close a structural supply deficit estimated to reach 18% by 2027 given the 15-to-20-year lead time from discovery to production. The World Nuclear Association projects reactor uranium requirements to more than double by 2040, driven by Small Modular Reactors and new entrants including Microsoft, while spot uranium has rebounded to US$82 per pound on tightening sentiment.

headline: GOLD CLIMBS TO $4,348 AS POST-FOMC MOMENTUM HOLDS — BANK OF AMERICA MARKS $4,360 AS 2026 AVERAGE TARGET
snippet: Gold spot touched $4,352 per ounce early September 16 before settling near $4,348, extending a post-FOMC rally that has added approximately $60 to the metal since Tuesday's well-anticipated Federal Reserve 25-basis-point hike and neutral forward guidance — placing gold squarely on top of Bank of America's trimmed 2026 average target of $4,360, while Goldman Sachs holds a higher year-end target of $4,900. Physical demand remains firm with Asian central bank accumulation continuing at a pace consistent with IMF Q2 2026 reserve data.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH EXPORT CONTROL PAUSE EXPIRES NOV 10 — WEST HAS 55 DAYS TO CLOSE THE REFINING GAP
snippet: Fastmarkets analysis published September 15 maps the countdown to November 10, when the one-year suspension of China's expanded rare earth export controls — introduced October 2025 and paused following the Xi-Trump trade framework — is scheduled to expire, potentially re-imposing licensing requirements on additional elements, foreign-manufactured products containing Chinese rare earths, and the refining and recycling technologies themselves. With no public signal from Beijing on an extension, the piece frames the processing stage as the principal Western vulnerability — China continues to handle the majority of global rare earth refining even as alternative mining sources develop — and identifies defence, AI infrastructure, and clean energy as the most exposed downstream industries.

headline: GOLDSEEK: MINING STOCKS AT INFLATION-DATA INFLECTION — ANALYST MAPS BUY ZONES AS FED RATE CYCLE TURNS
snippet: GoldSeek's September 13 analysis examines how the combined sequence of U.S. inflation reports and the September 15-16 FOMC meeting set up a technical inflection point for gold mining stocks — mapping specific buy zones for major miners and indices against the backdrop of what the author frames as a post-peak-rate environment where real rates begin to ease and earnings leverage to $4,300-plus gold becomes the dominant variable. The piece identifies the 12-week pattern of GDX relative-strength resets as the setup that has historically preceded the sector's most powerful sector runs.
